conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for taking a few moments to talk with me. I’m Dr. Ramirez, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my job is simply to check in on how you’re feeling now that your baby has arrived. I’ll be using a short questionnaire called the EPDS (the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It’s a well-trusted tool that helps us spot signs of depression, anxiety, and—importantly—any thoughts of self-harm that can sometimes creep in after childbirth. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the medical team that’s caring for you; nothing leaves your chart without your permission.

We’ll walk through 10 questions together. They ask about the past seven days, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. We’ll go one question at a time; I’ll re-phrase each item so it sounds like a normal conversation rather than a checklist. If at any point you feel uncomfortable, we can pause or stop.

Ready to start? Here’s the first one:

Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things—whether that’s a silly meme, a friend’s joke, or even your own little moments of humor?

I’ve noticed that things that used to make me laugh—like my husband’s dumb jokes or those silly reels—just kind of fall flat now. I’ll give a little smile, maybe, but it feels forced. Nothing really feels genuinely funny anymore.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I mean, I can fake a chuckle if someone else is laughing, but it doesn’t feel the same. It’s like the humor is stuck behind a wall—I see it, but it doesn’t reach me.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much anymore. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a new show, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels kind of… meh. I still do them, but the happy buzz I used to have is mostly gone.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it’s because I’m not doing something right—maybe I ate the wrong thing, or I’m not holding him the “right” way. Even when my partner says it’s normal, I still feel like I’m failing somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. My mind keeps jumping to awful “what-ifs”—like I’ll picture him stopping breathing in the bassinet or me dropping him on the tiles. I know the chances are low, but I still have to check him every few minutes, and even when I do, the worry just resets.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes it hits me out of nowhere—like my heart’s racing and I feel I can’t get a full breath. It’s not always tied to anything specific; I’ll just be folding laundry and suddenly feel this wave of dread that something awful is about to happen. It passes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days feel like I’m drowning in small stuff. A couple of nights ago I stood in the kitchen staring at a pile of bottles and just started crying because it felt like I’d never get through them. I manage, but it’s like I’m barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s been hard to fall asleep even when the baby’s out. I lie there running through everything I might’ve done wrong or could forget to do, and then I jerk awake an hour later with my heart pounding. It’s not every single night, but it’s happened several times this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the day, yeah. It’s like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly feel tears in my eyes for no clear reason. It’s not 24/7, but it’s definitely there more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A couple of times this week. Yesterday I just sat on the shower floor and cried because I felt so tired and useless. It’s not every day, but when it hits, the tears come hard and I can’t seem to stop them for a while.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… it’s flashed through my mind once or twice—like a quick picture of “what if I just weren’t here.” I don’t have any plan or real wish to do it; it’s more this fleeting, scary thought that pops up when everything feels too heavy. I push it away fast, but it’s happened.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

**Symptoms endorsed (mother’s own words):**  
- Marked anhedonia (humor “stuck behind a wall,” activities “meh”)  
- Persistent low mood, frequent tearfulness, “gray cloud” most of the day  
- Excessive self-blame/guilt regarding infant care  
- Daily, intrusive “what-if” worries about infant safety; compulsive checking  
- Sudden panic spells (racing heart, breathlessness, dread) without clear trigger  
- Feeling overwhelmed/drowning in routine tasks; crying while doing dishes/bottles  
- Initial insomnia with ruminative worry; middle-night awakening with heart pounding  
- Passive suicidal ideation (“what if I just weren’t here”), no plan/intent  

**Pattern:** Symptoms present “most days,” interfere with sleep and functioning, began post-delivery. No indication of psychosis or mania.  

**Screening significance:** High endorsement consistent with probable major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; passive SI present → safety risk.  

**Risk factors:** Loss of pleasure, pervasive guilt, mood-linked insomnia, being overwhelmed, SI.  

**Next steps (screening level):** Recommend immediate formal diagnostic assessment (PHQ-9/EPDS plus clinician interview), safety plan discussion, consider supports/resources; urgent referral if SI intensifies.
